original_prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}(4-2x)$ at the point $(1,\operatorname{ln}2).$
original_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=\operatorname{ln}u,\,u=4-2x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\cdot (-2) \\  & =\frac{1}{4-2x}\cdot (-2) \\  & =-\frac{2}{4-2x} \\  & =-\frac{\cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}\cdot (2-x)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2-x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line at the point where $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={-\frac{1}{2-x}|}_{x=1}=-\frac{1}{2-1}=-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(1,\operatorname{ln}2)$ is $m=-1.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-\operatorname{ln}2 & =-1(x-1) \\ y & =-x+1+\operatorname{ln}2\end{aligned}
$$

original_prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x+1)$ at the point $(0,0).$
original_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=\operatorname{ln}⁡u,\,u=3x+1.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{1}{3x+1}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{3}{3x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line at the point where $x=0$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={\frac{3}{3x+1}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{3}{3(0)+1} \\  & =3\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(0,0)$ is $m=3.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =3\cdot (x-0) \\ y & =3x\end{aligned}
$$

original_prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $f(x)=ln⁡(2-x)$ at the point $(1,0).$
original_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=ln⁡u,\,u=2-x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\cdot (-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2-x}\cdot (-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line at the point where $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={\frac{1}{x-2}|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{(1)-2} \\  & =-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(1,0)$ is $m=-1.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =(-1)\cdot (x-1) \\ y & =-x+1\end{aligned}
$$

original_prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $f(x)=4ln⁡(2x)$ at the point $(4,4ln⁡8).$
original_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=4ln⁡u,\,u=2x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{4}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{4}{u}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{4}{2x}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{8}{2x} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{2}\cdot 4}{\cancel{2}\cdot x} \\  & =\frac{4}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line at the point where $x=4$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & ={\frac{4}{x}|}_{x=4}=\frac{4}{4}=1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(4,4ln⁡8)$ is $m=1.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4ln⁡(8) & =1(x-4) \\ y & =x-4+4ln⁡(8)\end{aligned}
$$

original_prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $f(x)=12\ln(2 x)$ at the point $(12,12 \log{\left(24 \right)}).$
original_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$ f=12\ln u,\,u=2 x.$$

Differentiating gives

$$\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{12}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} &=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ &=\frac{12}{u}\cdot(2) \\ &=\frac{12}{2 x}\cdot(2) \\ &=\frac{12}{x}.\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line at the point where $x=12$ is

$$m=\left.(\frac{12}{x})\right|_{x=12}=1.$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(12,12 \log{\left(24 \right)})$ is $m=1.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$\begin{aligned}y-y_1 &=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(12 \log{\left(24 \right)}) &=(1)(x-(12)) \\ y &=x - 12 + 12 \log{\left(24 \right)}.\end{aligned}$$

original_prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $f(x)=\ln(21 - x)$ at the point $(20,0).$
original_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$ f=\ln u,\,u=21 - x.$$

Differentiating gives

$$\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1.$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} &=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ &=\frac{1}{u}\cdot(-1) \\ &=\frac{1}{21 - x}\cdot(-1) \\ &=\frac{1}{x - 21}.\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line at the point where $x=20$ is

$$m=\left.(\frac{1}{x - 21})\right|_{x=20}=-1.$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(20,0)$ is $m=-1.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$\begin{aligned}y-y_1 &=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(0) &=(-1)(x-(20)) \\ y &=20 - x.\end{aligned}$$
